title: Records, lists, detail pages, forms

fixtures.$comment: AREA-LEVEL standing fixtures. An item opts in with fixtures.provisioning = { use: "<key>", why: "…" }; the recipe is written ONCE here so several items do not carry drifting copies of the same sequence. Recipes are runtime-provisioned (no repo file is touched, nothing to seed, nothing to un-seed beyond the teardown line) and every call below is grounded in framework source at the cited file:line — replay them literally, and if one 4xxs, re-read the citation before assuming the recipe rotted.

qa-feeds-disabled.title: Scratch feeds-DISABLED parent (qa_nofeeds) — the FEEDS_DISABLED probe target
qa-feeds-disabled.why: Stock showcase declares NO object with `enable.feeds: false`. Feeds is opt-OUT (spec default true, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts), so every showcase object has comments ON and there is no naturally-occurring disabled parent to borrow — the opposite of the files case, where opt-IN (default false) leaves most objects files-disabled incidentally and attachments-storage could probe showcase_account before qa_nofiles existed. Without this recipe BOTH FEEDS_DISABLED clauses of record-discussion-mentions are blocked(fixture) and the code survives in that item's `negative` list alone — named but never driven, which is the gap #12118 was filed against.
qa-feeds-disabled.provenance: #12118 — the gap was measured from PR #12116 (the files-side twin, which added the FILES_DISABLED update-verb probe and reported this one rather than widening). Recipe shape copied from qa-scratch-authz in areas/attachments-storage.json (#7716/#7670) rather than invented.
requires: an admin session that holds the `manage_metadata` capability — PUT /api/v1/meta/:type/:name is capability-gated per ADR-0066 D1 (#6603), so a bare authenticated session is NOT enough (packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts, the `PUT /api/v1/meta/:type/:name` row)
an isolated boot (own port + file DB, dogfood skill §0) — this recipe authors metadata into the running app

AuditPlugin active in the boot: it owns sys_comment AND registers the enable.feeds capability gate (packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts). A boot without it accepts every comment and both probes go green for the wrong reason — confirm the gate is live before scoring either clause.

sequence.expect: 2xx with the installed package echoed back. A re-run against a live DB 409s on the duplicate id — send `overwrite: true` deliberately rather than adding it by reflex (the guard exists so a second install never silently clobbers the first).
sequence.source: POST /api/v1/packages is the dispatcher install route (packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts#packages note; client `packages.install`); the body shape { manifest, enableOnInstall?, overwrite? } is URL- and body-pinned in packages/client/src/client.test.ts

sequence.expect: 2xx. `enable.feeds` is stated EXPLICITLY false — unlike files it cannot be omitted, because omission means the spec default `true` (object.zod.ts) and would give a feeds-ENABLED object that scores both probes green for the wrong reason. `sharingModel` is public_read_write ON PURPOSE: the probes must be refused by the CAPABILITY gate, not by record access, and a caller who can read and edit this parent isolates FEEDS_DISABLED from the sibling RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE refusal (packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-access-hooks.ts).
sequence.source: `enable.feeds` is the #2707 opt-out, default true (packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts#Record: 'Record comments/collaboration feed. Default on; explicit false hides the feed UI and rejects any write that makes a comment target this object (403 FEEDS_DISABLED) — a new comment and an update that re-threads an existing one alike'). `sharingModel` is a TOP-LEVEL object key, enum ['private','public_read','public_read_write','controlled_by_parent'] (packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts#sharingModel; ADR-0090 D4 — re-pointed #18104: query is not a key this schema declares, and sharingModel is the key this sentence is about). `?package=` is read as `query.package` and threaded to saveMetaItem as packageId (packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts)

qa-feeds-disabled.teardown: DELETE /api/v1/packages/com.objectstack.qa.feeds (client `packages.uninstall`, ledgered at rest-route-ledger.ts) — or simply discard the isolated file DB, which is the cheaper path and the one an isolated boot makes free. Any throwaway qa_nofeeds record and any sys_comment row created against it go with the package.
knownGaps: The recipe lands the OBJECT only. Each probe inserts its own throwaway qa_nofeeds record inline (it needs that record's id in the thread_id), exactly as attachments-storage's clause 5 does with qa_nofiles — no standing rows here.

This recipe provisions the SERVER-side probe target. The `feeds:false must HIDE the panel` half of the negative is a console/objectui assertion: to score it, navigate to the qa_nofeeds record detail and confirm no discussion panel mounts and no sys_comment fetch is issued. If the console has no route for a scratch object in the running build, record that half blocked(fixture) and score the two API clauses — do not infer the UI half from the API refusal.

items.title: Create → read → update → delete a record through the console UI

requires: showcase_account — writable standard object (sharingModel public_read_write), required name + status, format validations tax_id_format / billing_email_format (examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/account.object.ts)

provisioning.why: supplies the persona clause 7 (clone is RLS-gated) rests on, and the non-owner cloner clause 6's ownership half needs (cloning a seeded showcase_field_zoo row, acceptance[6].verify) — a reader for whom a SOURCE row is invisible. showcase_account, the object the rest of this item drives, is public_read_write, so no persona can fail to read a row on it and the clause is unscoreable there; clause 7 is driven on showcase_invoice against INV-1003 (linus@example.com's) instead. Without the recipe the clause scores blocked(fixture) — which is what the 17.1.0 sweep recorded after reaching for the seeded demo personas and cloning showcase_account as Mei, who reads it fine (#10236).

knownGaps: Clause 7 (clone is RLS-gated) cannot be scored on showcase_account, the object every other clause here drives: it is public_read_write, so there is no persona for whom a source row is invisible. It needs showcase_invoice plus a contributor-bound member — the recipe qa-contributor-bound-member, which areas/search.json owns. That reference now lives in fixtures.provisioning as the AREA-QUALIFIED `search:qa-contributor-bound-member`, and check:platform-checklist RESOLVES it (#10593 gap 2, maintainer ruling 2026-08-22 — option A): both spellings are valid, an own-area key and `<area>:<recipe>` for one another area owns. So this is a real opt-in rather than a prose pointer — rename or move the recipe and this item fails the gate by name, instead of leaving a sentence aimed at nothing. ⛔ Replay it from areas/search.json; do not fork a second copy into this area.

no pin scores a full clause of this item at its layer (RUNNER rule 6, a pin scores only the layer it drives), so the item carries no automated ref. packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.readonly-insert.test.ts ('cloneData forwards the copied row AND the caller overrides whole — and reports the engine’s verdict on both') drives cloneData over a stub engine: the source's readonly column travels to engine.insert whole, the 201 body's droppedFields names it, and the clone's record does not carry it, which pins the protocol's delegation. packages/objectql/src/engine-insert-static-readonly-strip.test.ts drives a real ObjectQL engine over a recording driver, with no HTTP: a non-system caller's readonly key is stripped on create and falls back to the field's defaultValue, which pins the engine's strip. That is evidence for acceptance[6]'s readonly half at those two layers, never its pass. automated may return when a pin clones a row carrying a readonly value through the HTTP clone door and reads the clone back

steps: sign in as seeded admin; open Accounts via its nav entry (/_console/apps/com.example.showcase/showcase_account)
click New; fill name with a distinctive value (os-qa-<runid>), industry, status=active; leave website empty; Save

capture the create request/response (expect POST /api/v1/data/showcase_account). The payload also carries the select defaults of fields the step leaves untouched — sales_region:'amer' (its AMER option is default:true, examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/account.object.ts) — so expect that key in the body you diff (QA run #24556)
re-read server-side: GET /api/v1/data/showcase_account?$filter=[["name","=","os-qa-<runid>"]] — field-by-field vs the submitted payload
open the record detail; edit exactly one field (annual_revenue); Save; capture the PATCH /api/v1/data/showcase_account/<id>; re-read the full row via GET /api/v1/data/showcase_account/<id>
open the record's History tab (screenshot first, then read entries)

clone the record: POST /api/v1/data/showcase_account/<id>/clone (optionally with {overrides:{name:'os-qa-<runid>-clone'}}); capture the 201 result (new id ≠ source, sourceId, record); re-read the clone via GET /api/v1/data/showcase_account/<new id>

RLS probe on clone: as a persona WITHOUT read on the source row (a permission-zoo persona, or a non-owner under owner-RLS), POST the same clone route and capture the refusal — expect 404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND, never a silent duplicate (record blocked(fixture) if no non-reading persona is bound on this boot)

delete via the row/detail action; confirm the dialog; re-read via the filtered GET. ⚠️ If clause 7's recipe gave the member an own-row invoice pointing at THIS account, the delete answers 409 DELETE_RESTRICTED: the invoice's account lookup is required, and the engine turns a required set_null into restrict (packages/objectql/src/engine.ts). Point that invoice at a seeded account instead (the recipe's step 5 says so)
reload the list view and confirm final state

acceptance.clause: create returns success with an id and the API re-read shows every submitted value verbatim (no silent coercion/loss on any field)
acceptance.verify: field-by-field diff of the POST payload (the form's defaulted keys such as sales_region:'amer' included — steps[2]) vs the filtered GET re-read; the empty optional (website) stays empty, not defaulted

acceptance.clause: the update persists ONLY the edited field — untouched fields byte-identical across before/after full-row reads
acceptance.verify: diff of GET /api/v1/data/showcase_account/<id> before and after the single-field annual_revenue edit

acceptance.clause: delete removes the row authoritatively — the filtered API re-read returns 0 rows and the reloaded list no longer shows it
acceptance.verify: GET ...?$filter=[["name","=","os-qa-<runid>"]] returns total 0 post-delete

acceptance.clause: the list reflects each mutation after a full reload with correct display values (grid repaint is NOT the oracle — the reload is)
acceptance.verify: post-reload screenshots of the list at create and at delete

acceptance.clause: record History reflects the create and the update with display values (option labels, localized dates, real actor), not raw audit payloads or phantom value→null rows
acceptance.verify: after a screenshot confirms the History tab rendered, read its entries — same contract objectui e2e/live/record-history-display.spec.ts pins on showcase_account, the showcase's enable.trackHistory object (its option labels, the localized Customer Since date and the resolved owner; objectui blob 7ebc45106cff at the console pin cf153eb2e535)

acceptance.clause: unicode round-trips: a create with a CJK name (e.g. os-qa-<runid>-华宁) reads back byte-identical and is findable via list quick-search
acceptance.verify: filtered GET returns the CJK name unmangled; $search finds it (the seed's 华宁科技 proves the pattern — ADR-0061)

acceptance.clause: clone (POST /data/:object/:id/clone, gated by enable.clone default-on) returns 201 with a NEW id and the source's field VALUES copied, but engine-owned columns (id, audit, autonumber, formula, summary) and readonly columns RE-DERIVED not carried, and the clone is owned by the CLONER — not the source's owner. ⚠️ The readonly half is UNOBSERVABLE on the stock seed: showcase_account declares no readonly column, no showcase object has an approval_status, and the showcase's one readonly field (showcase_contact.lead_score) is null on every seeded row, so carried and re-derived read identically. Drive that half at this clause's own layer, the clone door, on a source row whose readonly value the run planted in its own file DB (verify). A run that does not plant one records that half blocked(fixture), never pass, and never off two reads that agree only because the column is null. The pins fixtures.knownGaps[1] names are evidence of their own layers only (RUNNER rule 6). The value has to be planted, because the server drops a readonly column a caller sets over HTTP (`x-objectstack-dropped-fields: lead_score;reason=readonly`, QA run #21782)
acceptance.verify: the 201 result carries {id (new ≠ sourceId), sourceId, record}; field-by-field diff shows business values copied and system/readonly columns re-derived (#3043 CLONE_STRIP_FIELDS + the engine's create-side static-readonly strip, #14147); owner_id resolves to the signed-in cloner (the clone is a create in the caller's context — packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts cloneData). ⚠ The owner half needs a cloner who is NOT the source's owner: the admin cloning a row the admin created reads the same owner_id either way (QA run #24572). Drive it as the provisioned contributor-bound member cloning a seeded showcase_field_zoo row (QA run #24572's suggestion, source-derived and not yet run — record the substitution): showcase_contributor grants allowCreate there (not on showcase_account, which it may only read; examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts), the zoo is public_read_write, and the same clone shows f_autonumber and f_formula re-derived. The readonly half: with the server stopped, write a value into one seeded showcase_contact row's lead_score in the run's own file DB with node:sqlite (no sqlite3 CLI in this container), `UPDATE showcase_contact SET lead_score = 42 WHERE id = 'ID'`, which reports one changed row; restart, read the row back over GET /api/v1/data/showcase_contact/ID (lead_score 42), then POST /api/v1/data/showcase_contact/ID/clone as the admin. The 201's droppedFields names lead_score with reason readonly (cloneData forwards the copy whole to engine.insert and reports the engine's onFieldsDropped verdict, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts), and a GET of the clone carries no lead_score value: the field declares no defaultValue to fall back to (examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/contact.object.ts). Derived from source, not replayed here
acceptance.evidence: clone response + source-vs-clone field diff + owner_id read; for the readonly half, the planted source read, the 201's droppedFields and the clone's lead_score read (or that half's blocked(fixture), with the knownGaps[1] pins beside it)

acceptance.clause: clone is RLS-gated: the source is fetched in the caller's context (engine.findOne with context), so cloning a record the caller cannot SEE is refused with 404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND — never a silent duplicate of an invisible row
acceptance.verify: ⚠️ NOT on showcase_account — it is public_read_write, so no persona can fail to read a source row there and the clause is unscoreable on the object the rest of this item drives. Drive it on showcase_invoice with a contributor-bound member (recipe qa-contributor-bound-member, owned by areas/search.json and opted into by this item as `search:qa-contributor-bound-member` — see fixtures.provisioning; replay it from there rather than forking a copy): as that member, POST the clone route against INV-1003 (linus@example.com's, invisible to them) → 404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND and no new row lands (recordNotFoundError from the null findOne). ⛔ Distinguish the two refusals before scoring: 404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND means the caller cannot SEE the source (this clause); 403 PERMISSION_DENIED means they can see it but hold no create grant — a DIFFERENT gate, and the one a persona with read-but-not-create hits. The 17.1.0 sweep hit exactly that confusion by cloning showcase_account as Mei, who reads it fine (#10236). Separately, an enable.clone:false object refuses with 403 CLONE_DISABLED
acceptance.evidence: the 404 RLS refusal with its code shown (not merely its status), the premise read proving the source row was invisible to that persona first, and a post-attempt count showing no new row

negative: save with the required Account Name empty → the form blocks with a named field error AND no row is created (filtered API count stays 0) — a silent success is a FAIL. ⛔ Not the Lifecycle (status) select: it offers no empty option and defaults to Prospect, so a status-empty save cannot be staged in the form

a clone that carries over the source's id / audit columns / an autonumber / a readonly approval_status instead of re-deriving them is a FAIL (#3043 — a clone must not mint an already-approved record); a clone of an RLS-invisible source that SUCCEEDS (200/201 with a new row) is a FAIL — the findOne runs in the caller's context precisely to refuse it

a direct API POST missing a required field that has NO default — on showcase_account that is `name` (QA run #24572) — → 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with fields[] carrying code 'required' (server enforces, not just the form — packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts). ⛔ Do NOT drive this on showcase_account: its status is required:true but the 'prospect' option carries default:true (data/objects/account.object.ts), so the default satisfies the requirement and the row is created with status:'prospect' — a 201 here is CORRECT behaviour, not a missing server guard. Pick a required field with no defaulted option, or record the substitution
a create with tax_id violating the tax_id_format rule → named validation error, never a silently-stored bad value

items.title: Field-type matrix: every FieldTypeSchema member renders its widget, accepts a valid value, round-trips over HTTP, and rejects invalid input

requires: showcase_field_zoo — one field of (almost) every FieldType (examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/field-zoo.object.ts); seeded rows 'Specimen — Full' and 'Specimen — Minimal'
knownGaps: summary is NOT on the zoo (a roll-up needs a child object and the zoo is a leaf) — verify it on its real carriers showcase_invoice.total and showcase_expense_report.total_amount/approved_amount instead
f_user / f_users / f_owner cannot be seeded or written on a fresh boot with no signed-up users (sys_user rows come from sign-up, not seeds) — assign after creating a user, or record blocked(fixture)

STALE on a CLI boot (QA run #24616): f_secret writes fail closed only when no ICryptoProvider is registered (ADR-0100), and `os dev` / `serve` wire a LocalCryptoProvider on every boot (packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, the secret-field crypto wiring: 'Dev/self-host gets a LocalCryptoProvider'), so a raw PATCH of f_secret answers 200 and reads back masked. Only a host composed WITHOUT that provider refuses the write — there, verify the masked-read contract via the dogfood pin

steps: run the pinned HTTP round-trip matrix: pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run test/field-zoo-roundtrip.dogfood.test.ts (write vectors + expected read shapes live in test/field-zoo.matrix.ts)
boot the showcase on its own port and DB; open Field Zoo (/_console/apps/com.example.showcase/showcase_field_zoo) and open 'Specimen — Full' in edit mode; screenshot the form before reading DOM

enumerate the rendered control for every f_* field and build a variant→widget table (date→date input, color→color input, richtext / markdown / html / code→their dedicated field widgets, select/multiselect→pickers, image/file→upload, location/address→structured inputs, rating/slider/progress→their own controls, formula→read-only). f_autonumber is NOT on the form at all: the field is readonly by construction (Field.autonumber sets readonly: true, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts) and objectui's auto-form drops schema-readonly fields in create AND edit mode (plugin-form autoLayout.ts filterSystemFields) — read it on the record detail page instead. At the console pin the richtext, markdown, html and code widgets are textarea-based BY DESIGN (objectui packages/fields/src/widgets/RichTextField.tsx / CodeField.tsx: a Textarea inside the dedicated widget, with its own label and controls): record that as the dedicated widget, not as a generic text input
through the form, change one representative value per family (a select, an array type, a temporal, a structured JSON), Save, and capture the PATCH
re-read the record via GET /api/v1/data/showcase_field_zoo/<id> and diff against the submitted values (arrays compared as sets)
POST an out-of-set select value (f_select: 'not-a-value') directly to /api/v1/data/showcase_field_zoo and capture the refusal
POST f_lookup with a fabricated account id and capture the refusal (#4441 dangling-reference gate)
verify f_formula and f_autonumber materialized server-side on a created row (formula = f_number × f_percent / 100)

an EXPORT GRANT for the exporting principal, which no stock set carries: allowExport is opt-in (packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts#resolveUserExportAllowed, export = read ∧ a set saying allowExport: true), and no stock permission set grants it, the admin wildcard included (#3544). Without it the seeded admin sees no Export control and GET /api/v1/data/showcase_task/export answers 403 EXPORT_NOT_PERMITTED. Provision one before step 6: author a runtime set through the metadata door, PUT /api/v1/meta/permission/qa_task_export with {name:'qa_task_export', label, objects:{showcase_task:{allowRead:true, allowExport:true}}} (published; a ?mode=draft save also needs its POST …/publish), then bind it with POST /api/v1/data/sys_user_permission_set {user_id: <admin id>, permission_set: 'qa_task_export'} — the grant names its set by NAME (ADR-0131 D4) — and reload so /me/permissions carries the merged map

items.title: Form-view gallery: every FormViewSchema layout type renders and submits

requires: showcase_task's default form (type simple — the `form` key) and its formViews tabbed / wizard / split / quick (drawer) — examples/app-showcase/src/ui/views/task.view.ts. The console reads ONLY the default (objectDef.form ?? formViews.default — RecordFormPage, resolveFormViewLayout), so a named formViews entry is reachable from no console door: each page-level variant is reached by overlaying the object's default form with that variant's type + sections (view is org-overridable, ADR-0005) and reverting afterwards. The overlay recipe: PUT /api/v1/meta/view/showcase_task.form?mode=draft with the ViewItem {name:'showcase_task.form', object:'showcase_task', viewKind:'form', isDefault:true, config:{type:<variant>, sections:<that variant's sections>}}, then POST /api/v1/meta/view/showcase_task.form/publish. Each variant's sections can be read from its own served view item — the container serves formViews as showcase_task.tabbed / .wizard / .split / .quick (GET /api/v1/meta/view/showcase_task.<variant>, QA run #24572). ⚠ Item-level isDefault:true is REQUIRED: the console takes an object's default form — what /new and /edit render — ONLY from a form ViewItem that carries it (objectui packages/app-shell/src/providers/MetadataProvider.tsx applyViewItem, objectui#11539). Without it the publish succeeds, the flag is gone from the served row, and the page falls back to the all-fields layout, which reads like 'the variant does not render'

examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/task-desk.page.ts — the presentation surface: a JSX page whose ObjectForm opens with formType="drawer" (edit, a side panel) and formType="modal" (create, a dialog) over the task list
knownGaps: no form view in the showcase authors the spec's 6th form type, 'modal' (coverage.ts FORM_VIEW_TYPES deliberately lists 5). A modal-PRESENTED form exists on task-desk.page.ts (ObjectForm formType="modal", create), which is where the modal variant is scored; if that page cannot be reached, record the modal variant blocked(fixture) rather than ticking or silently skipping it

drawer and modal are presentation modes, not page layouts (ADR-0050, Proposed): the metadata record-form page renders an authored type drawer/modal as simple BY DESIGN (RecordFormPage — the form-layout-vs-presentation note on objectstack#1890), and the New/Edit modal maps only tabbed (resolveFormViewLayout — wizard/split degrade to a stacked section list there). So the page-level layouts are walked on the page routes (/new and /record/:id/edit, both RecordFormPage), and the presentations on task-desk.page.ts

steps: open a task record's full-page edit form (…/showcase_task/record/<id>/edit — RecordFormPage) on the stock default form (type simple); screenshot; verify the declared section ('Task', 2 columns) and its field order

overlay the default form with the tabbed variant (type tabbed + the sections of formViews.tabbed, through the fixtures.requires[0] recipe with item-level isDefault:true); reopen the page form; verify the three tabs (Overview / Schedule / Details) and that switching tabs preserves entered values

overlay the default form with the wizard variant; open the PAGE form (…/showcase_task/new, or the record's /edit route — RecordFormPage passes the type in both modes); walk Basics → Assignment → Schedule with next/back; verify back preserves values and submit happens ONCE at the end. The New/Edit MODAL renders a wizard as a stacked section list by design (resolveFormViewLayout), so the steps are walked on the page route

requires: showcase_invoice_line rules (examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/invoice.object.ts): description requiredWhen record.quantity >= 100 (ROW-scoped); product/quantity/unit_price readonlyWhen parent.status == 'paid' (PARENT-scoped); receipt Field.file upload cell (objectui#2360)

a draft invoice with editable lines (INV-1002) and a paid one (INV-1003); for clause 5, INV-1002 must carry a SECOND line with a DISTINCT stored position. The stock INV-1002 ships one line, and a line added through the data API with no position defaults to 0, which collides with the first; seed it with position 1, or any value the first line does not hold — AND with its `amount` (quantity × unit_price): amount is computed in the client and stored as sent (examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/invoice.object.ts, the amount field's comment), so a line staged over the data API without it carries amount null and the invoice total ignores it (QA run #24616). Or add the line through the grid, which computes it. On an invoice whose lines share a stored position the grid legitimately re-emits the sibling's position on save: it stamps row[sortField] = index on every change (GridField), with the sort field deriveDetail picks from the child (position)

items.title: Concurrent edits collide loudly (OCC 409 + conflict dialog), never silent last-write-wins; inline two-surface edit is ONE atomic OCC-guarded save
personas: seeded admin (admin@objectos.ai / admin123) in TWO independent browser sessions (distinct auth cookies), 'A' and 'B'

requires: any writable object whose rows carry an updated_at OCC token (e.g. showcase_account or showcase_task) — the form reads updated_at and sends it as If-Match (objectui plugin-form/src/occSave.tsx; framework packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts updateData If-Match handling)
a record with both a details-body field and a header-highlight field for the two-surface inline-edit fold-in (RecordDetailView highlight fields)
knownGaps: AUTOMATION IS PINNED IN THE objectui REPO, NOT HERE — `automated.ref` names objectui specs exclusively, so from this checkout the item is neither runnable nor pin-evidenced (no console bundle is built here and none of those specs exist here). Full protocol: RUNNER.md, the objectui-pinned-automation standing fact.

steps: open the SAME record's detail in session A and session B (both hold the same updated_at)
in A: edit one field, Save; capture the PATCH carrying If-Match: <updated_at> → 200; the record's updated_at advances
in B (still holding the STALE updated_at): edit the same field, Save; capture the response

assert B receives 409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE and the conflict dialog appears — on the modal edit form it is occSave's 'Save conflict' dialog offering Keep editing / Overwrite; on an inline edit it is the ConcurrentUpdateDialog offering Reload / Overwrite — NOT a silent overwrite, NOT a bare error

Reload lives on the INLINE-edit ConcurrentUpdateDialog (objectui plugin-detail), not on the modal form's dialog: drive this leg as an inline stale save — in B double-click the field on the record page, let A's write land, Save → 409 → choose Reload; the page refetches and shows A's value, and B sends no further write
in B re-edit and choose Overwrite → the retry re-keys ifMatch to the version the 409 reported → 200; re-read shows exactly one winner (B's value)

INLINE two-surface (§E1): on the detail, enter the shared inline-edit session; edit one details-BODY field AND one header-HIGHLIGHT field; confirm ONE Save bar; Save; capture the single PATCH and its keys + headers
stale-ifMatch inline path: repeat the inline save holding a stale updated_at (a concurrent write landed between) and capture the outcome

acceptance.clause: the losing save is REFUSED with 409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE server-side — never a silent last-write-wins that overwrites A with no signal
acceptance.verify: B's PATCH returns HTTP 409 with code CONCURRENT_UPDATE — the 409 mapping is packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts#structuredCodeAnswer (error.code CONCURRENT_UPDATE / ConcurrentUpdateError → 409, the current head as data), and the error class is packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts#ConcurrentUpdateError; A's value is intact on an independent re-read

acceptance.clause: the conflict surfaces a conflict DIALOG offering a structured choice — Keep editing / Overwrite on the modal edit form (occSave), Reload / Overwrite on an inline edit (ConcurrentUpdateDialog) — not a silent overwrite and not a raw stack trace
acceptance.verify: after screenshot, the ConcurrentUpdateDialog (plugin-detail) / occSave conflict dialog (plugin-form) renders with the racer's version and the two actions

acceptance.clause: on the inline-edit conflict dialog (the surface that offers it), Reload DISCARDS B's pending edit and refetches — the page then shows A's value
acceptance.verify: after Reload, the form's field equals A's saved value (a fresh GET), and no B write landed

acceptance.clause: Overwrite re-keys ifMatch to the version the 409 reported and lands EXACTLY ONE winner on re-read — an explicit last-write chosen by the user, not an accident
acceptance.verify: the overwrite retry carries the 409-reported currentVersion as ifMatch → 200; the final re-read shows B's value, with no lost-update ambiguity (occSave settle/retry path)

acceptance.clause: inline two-surface edit is ONE atomic save: editing one details-body field AND one header-highlight field drives ONE Save bar and issues ONE PATCH carrying EXACTLY those two keys plus ifMatch = the read updated_at (the draft holds changed keys only — never computed/readonly/untouched fields)
acceptance.verify: the single PATCH body has exactly the two edited keys and an If-Match header (objectui InlineEditSaveBar dataSource.update(obj,id,draft,{ifMatch:data.updated_at}); InlineEditContext draft = changed keys). No pin covers this clause: objectui e2e/live/inline-edit-polish-2572.spec.ts saves one field without If-Match

acceptance.clause: the inline path is OCC-guarded too: an inline save on a stale ifMatch → 409 conflict (same dialog), not a silent overwrite
acceptance.verify: the stale inline PATCH returns 409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE and the conflict dialog appears

negative: silent last-write-wins — B's save overwriting A with no 409 and no dialog — is THE FAIL this item exists to catch
an inline two-surface edit that issues TWO PATCHes (one per surface) or a single PATCH carrying untouched/computed/readonly keys is a FAIL — one atomic save, changed keys only
an inline or form save that omits the If-Match header (an unguarded write) is a FAIL — the OCC token must ride or a concurrent overwrite goes undetected

steps: as admin, open a record detail with the discussion panel (feeds enabled); screenshot
type a comment containing an @mention (the mention autocomplete offers mentionSuggestions); post it
observe the OPTIMISTIC comment row appear immediately; capture the sys_comment create

as the mentioned second user, open the notification bell — it gains the mention notification with a deep link back to the record; unreadCount increments; mark-as-read drops it. control for both probes — repeat the same two calls against a feeds-ENABLED parent (the seeded showcase record used above) and confirm they SUCCEED. A 403 that also fires on the enabled parent is measuring access, not the capability gate, and neither clause may be scored from it

acceptance.clause: PER-VARIANT: column RESIZE persists across a reload — the widths restore from the column-state store (localStorage grid-columns-<object>[-<view>], or a persisted view override). Column REORDER and PIN are not stock list-view personalizations, and the clause does not assert them there. ObjectGrid enables drag-reorder only from `reorderableColumns` (default false), which is an object-grid component prop (packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts#ObjectGridPropsSchema), not a ListView key. Pinning is AUTHOR-declared per column (`pinned`, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts#ListColumnSchema), with no runtime pin control, and the persisted column state carries widths and order, never pins. So: reorder persists across a reload only on a grid that enables it (score it there, or record n/a on the stock showcase_task list view); a column the view declares `pinned` renders pinned after the reload (n/a when the view declares none, as the stock task views do)
acceptance.verify: after a screenshot confirms render, the reloaded grid shows the same widths (ObjectGrid columnState priority: props override > localStorage > empty; saveColumnState persists widths and order only). The reorder and pin variants are judged as the clause scopes them

items.title: Record edit undo: toast Undo / Ctrl+Z restores the prior value through the API and logs a revert; undo after a concurrent change must not silently clobber
personas: a second session (for the concurrent-clobber probe)

requires: a writable record and an action that declares `undoable: true` with operation 'update' (a patch of one field) — at objectui 1fb1ced36243 the ONLY path that pushes an Undo op: useConsoleActionRuntime and RecordDetailView attach the toast Undo for `undoable` actions, while inline grid and form edits push none. objectui react/src/hooks/useGlobalUndo.ts + core globalUndoManager hold the stack. ⚠ The stock showcase declares NO undoable action (examples/app-showcase has zero `undoable` keys), and a runtime-authored action is not joined into the served object's actions[] (records-forms.action-location-matrix knownGaps), so the action must ship PACKAGED in the showcase — see `blocked`
knownGaps: AUTOMATION IS PINNED IN THE objectui REPO, NOT HERE — `automated.ref` names objectui specs exclusively, so from this checkout the item is neither runnable nor pin-evidenced (no console bundle is built here and none of those specs exist here). Drive it by hand in the browser and score it as a manual run, OR run the pin in an objectui checkout and cite the output naming the revision (17.1.0 sweep subject: 9a3daf8d37ad). ⛔ Never score it as covered on the strength of the `automated` field alone — an unrun pin is a claim, not evidence. Full protocol: RUNNER.md, the objectui-pinned-automation standing fact.

BLOCKED(fixture) on stock, all four clauses (QA run #23163, objectstack 36b2889c, objectui 1fb1ced36243). Inline edits push no Undo op at this pin — only actions declaring `undoable` do — and the showcase declares none, while a runtime-authored undoable action is not served. The item becomes runnable when examples/app-showcase ships a packaged undoable update action on a writable object (operation 'update' with a patch, so the Undo captures the prior value of every written field — ActionSchema.undoable in packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts). Lift `blocked` in the revision that names that fixture. ⛔ Do not score an inline edit's missing Undo as this item's FAIL: the console never offers one by design

steps: open a record; run the packaged undoable action (fixtures.requires[0]) on it; confirm the success toast shows an Undo button. An inline edit offers none by design
click Undo (or press Ctrl+Z); capture the resulting update; re-read the record over the API and confirm the prior value is restored
open the History/audit and confirm a revert entry was added (a forward write, not a silent rollback)
press Ctrl+Shift+Z (redo); confirm the edited value is restored
CONCURRENT-CLOBBER probe: in session A make the undoable edit; in session B change the SAME field and save; back in A, click Undo

Run-proven recipe (QA run #24616): on a scratch app copy, put every scratch hook on showcase_inquiry behind a name-prefix condition (record.name.startsWith('qa-…')) so it touches only the probe rows; for the fail-closed probe, `record.name.startsWith('qa-fc') && int(record.name) > 0` compiles and faults only for a 'qa-fc…' row
a real running server: hooks fire in the ObjectQL engine on the live /api/v1/data/* route, never on a simulated dispatch

acceptance.clause: a condition that cannot be evaluated FAILS CLOSED (#4775): the write is ABORTED, not silently skipped — and it is NOT softened by onError:'log' nor fire-and-forgotten, because the condition gate runs OUTSIDE the async/retry/onError wrappers
acceptance.verify: scratch hook whose condition COMPILES but cannot be evaluated at runtime (e.g. int(record.name) > 0, written to a row whose name is not numeric); a write to that object is refused and the row does not land (hook-wrappers.ts: conditionFn throws outside runWithErrorPolicy). The wire envelope is a coded refusal: 400 {code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR'}, whose error text names the hook and the CEL fault ("Hook 'NAME' could not evaluate its condition (FAULT) — operation aborted.") and never the condition source, and no '[REST] Unhandled error' line is logged for it (#24662 retired the generic 500 INTERNAL_ERROR that #24619 row (b) recorded). A 500 INTERNAL_ERROR here is a FAIL. An UNCOMPILABLE condition never reaches this gate: it is refused at authoring (PUT /api/v1/meta/hook → 422 INVALID_METADATA, expression-invalid), so it cannot stand in for the runtime fail-closed probe
acceptance.evidence: the refusal (status 400 + code VALIDATION_ERROR + the hook named in its error text) + a post-attempt count showing no row

acceptance.clause: two hooks on the SAME object+event run lowest-priority-first: scratch hooks at priority 10 and 90 log in that order on one write (hook-binder passes priority to engine.registerHook; the engine orders by it, lower first)

negative: a beforeInsert (or beforeDelete) hook that THROWS under onError:'abort' but leaves the row written (filtered count > 0) is a FAIL — abort must roll the WHOLE write back (the hef_ref_guard dogfood pin is the reference shape)
an async onError:'log' hook failure that ROLLS BACK the triggering write is a FAIL — fire-and-forget runs after the write resolved and can only be logged, never un-commit it

a SILENT no-fire on a real done:false→true transition is a FAIL — the audit MUST emit; if it truly did not, first rule out that the hooks registered (GET /api/v1/meta/hook) and that the async line was given time to settle before filing (seed-data-thin / async-settle)

the audit firing on a NON-transition edit of an already-done task is a FAIL — it would prove the condition collapsed from the two-root transition to a bare `record.done == true` state test (the exact #4784 regression)

an unevaluable condition that SILENTLY SKIPS (letting a before* guard through, or dropping an after* audit) instead of aborting the operation is a FAIL — #4775 fails closed, loudly, and onError never sees the condition error

items.title: Per-type CONSTRAINT enforcement on the write path (not just widget render): length/range/option/reference/computed limits, and where the platform deliberately does NOT enforce

requires: showcase_field_zoo (examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/field-zoo.object.ts): name text maxLength 200; f_number min 0 max 1000; f_currency scale 2 currencyConfig{precision 2} min 0; f_percent min 0 max 100; f_select {low,medium,high}; f_multiselect {red,green,blue}; f_lookup→showcase_account; f_master_detail→showcase_project; f_tree→showcase_field_zoo (self-reference); f_autonumber (default counter, NO autonumberFormat); f_formula = f_number*f_percent/100

showcase_invoice (invoice.object.ts): status select {draft,sent,paid,void} required; account lookup with lookupFilters status!=churned; total summary(sum showcase_invoice_line.amount) — the summary carrier the zoo lacks
knownGaps: precision/scale is DECLARED but NOT enforced on the write path — record-validator.ts validateOne's number branch checks only min/max/finite, no runtime reads field.scale/precision for rounding (grep clean across objectql/rest/runtime), and the SQL driver stores number/currency/percent as table.float (REAL affinity), not DECIMAL(p,s) (packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts#createColumn). A currency value with more decimals than `scale` is stored verbatim, unrounded. Record it as a gap; do NOT tick 'scale enforced'.

autonumberFormat TOKEN expansion ({0000}/{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}/{YYYYMMDD}/{field}, per-rendered-prefix scope+reset) has NO showcase fixture — no showcase object declares autonumberFormat (f_autonumber uses the default bare 4-width global counter). Token expansion is pinned instead by packages/spec/src/data/autonumber-format.test.ts + packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-autonumber.test.ts; only server-assignment + client-value-ignored is driveable on the zoo.

the #4441 reference gate is EXISTENCE-only and deliberately unscoped (engine.ts assertReferencesResolve) — an id that exists but lies outside the field's lookupFilters/dependsOn scope is accepted; scope enforcement is client-only (drilled in records-forms.cascading-multilevel-and-clear).

summary is a runtime-MAINTAINED cache, not a write-rejected readonly field — a caller-supplied initial total is a SUPPORTED import path and is kept, then self-heals to the child aggregate on the next child write (rule-validator.ts RUNTIME_OWNED_FIELD_TYPES note, #6014). Only `formula` is strictly read-only-on-write; do NOT assert 'summary rejects direct writes'.

steps: boot the showcase on its own port and DB; sign in as the seeded admin; capture an API token for direct /api/v1/data/* POST/PATCH/GET

STRING length: POST /api/v1/data/showcase_field_zoo with name = a 201-char string (maxLength 200) and capture the refusal; then POST a 200-char name and capture success — confirm the long value was NOT silently truncated-and-stored
NUMBER range: POST f_number = -1, then = 1001, then a non-number ('abc'); capture each refusal; POST f_number = 500 and re-read verbatim
SCALE (gap probe): POST f_currency = 1234.567 (declared scale 2); GET the row and record whether the stored value is rounded (expected: stored 1234.567 verbatim — NOT enforced)

SELECT server boundary: POST f_select = 'not-a-value' AND (second carrier) POST showcase_invoice status = 'archived'; capture both invalid_option refusals with their options[] echo; confirm neither row count grew

MULTISELECT shape: POST f_multiselect = 'red' (a scalar) and re-read as ['red'] (coerced to array); POST f_multiselect = {x:1} (a non-array object) → capture invalid_type; POST f_multiselect = ['red','purple'] → capture the per-element invalid_option naming 'purple'; POST ['red','blue'] → re-read as a set

REFERENCE: POST f_lookup = a fabricated account id → capture reference_not_found; POST f_lookup = a real seeded account id → re-read verbatim (note: an EXISTING but out-of-scope id is accepted — see cascading-multilevel-and-clear)

AUTONUMBER server-assigned: POST a row with f_autonumber = 'HACK-9999'; GET it and confirm the stored value is the engine's sequence number (client value dropped, #5503); PATCH f_autonumber on an existing row and confirm the change is dropped while the call returns success
FORMULA read-only: POST a row writing f_formula = 999 directly; GET and confirm f_formula equals f_number*f_percent/100 (the write was ignored); with f_number=42, f_percent=75 the read is 31.5

SUMMARY (nuance): create a showcase_invoice + lines; GET total and confirm it equals the line sum server-side; separately confirm a caller-supplied initial total on import is retained (maintained cache, not rejected) — do not treat summary as write-rejected

acceptance.clause: text/textarea/email/url/phone length is a REJECT, not a truncation: a value longer than the field's maxLength returns 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with fields[] {field, code:'max_length', constraint:{maxLength, actual}} and stores NOTHING — the over-length value is never silently truncated to fit
acceptance.verify: the 201-char name POST returns max_length naming maxLength 200 & actual 201; the row count does not grow; a 200-char name succeeds. Codes are the ADR-0114 FieldErrorCode catalog (packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts); enforcement in packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts validateOne string branch
acceptance.evidence: both refusal/success responses + before/after row counts

acceptance.clause: number/currency/percent range is bounded both sides server-side: below `min` → code 'min_value' {min}; above `max` → 'max_value' {max}; a non-finite value → 'invalid_number'; an in-range value round-trips verbatim
acceptance.verify: f_number (min 0 max 1000) rejects -1 (min_value) and 1001 (max_value) and 'abc' (invalid_number); 500 re-reads as 500. record-validator.ts validateOne number branch
acceptance.evidence: the three refusals + the in-range re-read

acceptance.clause: KNOWN GAP recorded, not ticked: `scale`/`precision` are NOT enforced on write — a currency value with more decimals than the declared scale is stored VERBATIM (float column, validator checks only min/max/finite). The run records the observed unrounded value as a gap and must NOT report 'scale enforced'
acceptance.verify: POST f_currency 1234.567 (scale 2) succeeds and GET returns 1234.567 unrounded — corroborated by record-validator.ts (no scale rounding) and sql-driver.ts createColumn (table.float, not DECIMAL). A run that shows rounding-to-2 would be a NEW enforcement to file, not a pass here
acceptance.evidence: the write response + the unrounded re-read

acceptance.clause: closed-set types reject a non-declared option value SERVER-side on at least two carriers (not just the widget): f_select and showcase_invoice.status each refuse an out-of-set value with code 'invalid_option' and an options[] listing the allowed set; the row count does not grow
acceptance.verify: direct POSTs f_select='not-a-value' and status='archived' both return invalid_option carrying options[]; record-validator.ts select/radio branch (allowed = optionValues(def.options))
acceptance.evidence: both refusal envelopes (with options[]) + before/after counts

acceptance.clause: multiselect storage/read shape is an ARRAY: a lone scalar is coerced to a 1-element array (normalizeMultiValueFields), a non-array object is rejected 'invalid_type', an element outside options is rejected 'invalid_option' echoing the offending element, and a valid array round-trips compared as a set
acceptance.verify: f_multiselect: 'red'→['red']; {x:1}→invalid_type; ['red','purple']→invalid_option naming 'purple'; ['red','blue']→set-equal on re-read. record-validator.ts multi-value branch + normalizeMultiValueFields

acceptance.clause: reference types (lookup/master_detail/tree/user) store the id verbatim and reject a DANGLING id with code 'reference_not_found' {target} for a non-system caller (#4441) — with the boundary that the gate is EXISTENCE-only: an id that exists but is out of lookupFilters/dependsOn scope is accepted (unscoped by design)
acceptance.verify: a fabricated f_lookup id → reference_not_found; a real seeded account id → verbatim re-read; engine.ts assertReferencesResolve + referenceExists (isSystem/readonly/caller-supplied narrowing). Pinned by packages/objectql/src/engine-lookup-referential-integrity.test.ts
acceptance.evidence: the dangling refusal + the verbatim re-read + a note that an out-of-scope existing id is accepted

acceptance.clause: autonumber is server-assigned and a client value is IGNORED on both write paths: a POSTed f_autonumber is replaced by the engine sequence value (stripRuntimeOwnedFields, #5503) and a PATCH of it is dropped — the call returns success while the column holds the generated number, never the forged one
acceptance.verify: POST f_autonumber='HACK-9999' re-reads as a sequence number, not 'HACK-9999'; PATCH is a no-op on the field. rule-validator.ts RUNTIME_OWNED_FIELD_TYPES=['autonumber'] + stripRuntimeOwnedFields/stripReadonlyFields. Pinned by packages/objectql/src/engine-autonumber-runtime-owned.test.ts
acceptance.evidence: the create re-read + the PATCH no-op re-read

acceptance.clause: formula is read-only/computed: a direct write to f_formula is ignored and the read equals f_number*f_percent/100 (42*75/100 = 31.5); summary is a runtime-MAINTAINED cache (invoice.total = Σ line.amount server-side) and is NOT write-rejected — a caller's initial total is a supported import path that self-heals on the next child write
acceptance.verify: GET f_formula after a direct write shows 31.5 (write ignored); GET showcase_invoice.total equals the seeded line sum. No pin reads invoice.total: objectui e2e/live/summary-rollup.spec.ts, cited here until revision 2, asserts a server roll-up on another carrier (showcase_project's total_estimate and task_count over showcase_task, written through a direct /api/v1/batch) and never reads showcase_invoice.total. The formula/summary distinction: rule-validator.ts note (formula computed-on-read; summary maintained cache, deliberately NOT in RUNTIME_OWNED)
acceptance.evidence: the formula re-read + the invoice total re-read

negative: a 201-char value silently TRUNCATED to 200 and stored with 200/201 is a FAIL — the contract is reject-not-truncate (max_length), and a truncating write corrupts the value with no signal
an out-of-set select/status value accepted with 200 is a FAIL — the record-validator, not the picker, is the boundary
a client-supplied f_autonumber persisted verbatim is a FAIL — a forged business identifier bypassing the sequence (#5503)
a currency value rounded to `scale` and reported as 'scale enforced' is a FALSE PASS — the platform does not round on write; the honest verdict is the recorded gap
a dangling lookup id accepted with 200 is a FAIL (#4441)

items.title: Cascade clear-semantics and the server boundary: stale-child clear on parent change, the WRITTEN-value server gate, and where cascade scope is client-only

requires: showcase_cascade (examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/cascading-select.object.ts): country → province, province dependsOn ['country'] with per-option visibleWhen (cn→zj/gd, us→ca/tx); sharingModel public_read_write

showcase_invoice.contact dependsOn ['account'] (invoice.object.ts) — the dependent LOOKUP twin; account carries lookupFilters status!=churned; seed spread Northwind/Contoso/Fabrikam (examples/app-showcase/src/data/seed/index.ts)
knownGaps: NO 3-level (grandparent→parent→child) dependsOn fixture exists in the showcase — the deepest chain is 2-level (country→province). The 'changing the grandparent clears/revalidates BOTH descendants' behavior cannot be driven; blocked on a fixture (a 3-level cascade object). The 2-level clear (clause 0) and the server WRITTEN-value gate (clause 1) are the driveable depth.

SELECT cascade server enforcement is WRITTEN-value-only: evaluateOptionVisibility re-checks a picked option only when that field is IN the write payload (rule-validator.ts: `!(name in data) continue`). A PATCH that changes ONLY the parent and omits the now-invalid child does NOT revalidate it server-side (clause 2) — server-side cascade integrity on the change-parent path depends entirely on the CLIENT clear. Recorded as a product gap.

LOOKUP cascade scope is NOT server-enforced at all: the #4441 reference gate (engine.ts assertReferencesResolve) is deliberately EXISTENCE-only/unscoped, so a directly-POSTed contact that belongs to a DIFFERENT account is accepted as long as the row exists (clause 4). dependsOn/lookupFilters is a picker-side narrowing; the only server reference guard is dangling→reference_not_found.

steps: boot the showcase on its own port and DB; sign in as the seeded admin; keep an API token for direct /api/v1/data/* writes

items.title: Secret/encrypted field: ciphertext at rest, masked on every read, no-op mask re-submit, and fail-CLOSED without an ICryptoProvider (ADR-0100)

requires: showcase_field_zoo.f_secret = Field.secret (encrypted-at-rest) and f_password = Field.password({ackPlaintextMasking:true}) (examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/field-zoo.object.ts)

a CryptoProvider-wired boot: `os serve` wires LocalCryptoProvider (AES-256-GCM, OS_SECRET_KEY or a persisted dev key) via engine.setCryptoProvider when the data engine + service-settings resolve (packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts) — so on a stock dev boot f_secret writes SUCCEED (ciphertext); sys_secret platform object must be registered
knownGaps: f_secret is NOT seeded (the Specimen rows omit it) — drive a live UI/API write to exercise the encrypt path.

the fail-CLOSED path has NO live leg on stock, of necessity (QA run #21784, parked on #22017 row 22). Every stock boot wires LocalCryptoProvider. The 'no OS_SECRET_KEY under the production guard' boot this note once suggested never comes up: LocalCryptoProvider refuses to start in production without a stable key, and serve.ts rethrows that refusal. A boot without @objectstack/service-settings is not a stock composition. So acceptance[3] is recorded blocked(fixture) on stock, citing this gap. packages/objectql/src/secret-fields.test.ts ('fail-closed: writing a secret field with no CryptoProvider throws': the write throws and neither store holds a row) is engine-layer evidence beside that verdict, never its pass (RUNNER rule 6, a pin scores only the layer it drives). The field-type-matrix's 'seed deliberately omits it' note is about SEEDING, not serve-time wiring.

inspecting the raw business-row column / sys_secret ciphertext needs DB access (file:/tmp/<run>/data.db) — where the API is the only surface, assert the mask on read + the absence of plaintext in any API response instead.

steps: boot the showcase on its own port and DB, on a provider-wired boot (`os serve`, LocalCryptoProvider); sign in as the seeded admin; keep an API token

WRITE ciphertext: POST /api/v1/data/showcase_field_zoo {name:'sec-1', f_secret:'topsecret-value'}; GET the row over the API and confirm f_secret reads back as the SECRET_MASK, never 'topsecret-value'; where DB access exists, confirm the business-row column holds a 'secret:<handle>' ref and the plaintext lives only (encrypted) in sys_secret
MASK on read for f_password too: POST f_password='p@ssw0rd!'; GET and confirm f_password reads back as the mask (generic password: plaintext-at-rest but masked-on-read)
ECHOED-MASK no-op: PATCH the row's f_secret back as the SECRET_MASK sentinel; GET and confirm the stored secret is UNCHANGED (a form round-trip re-submitting the mask does not wipe it)

FAIL-CLOSED: on a boot with NO CryptoProvider registered (deliberately unwired), POST f_secret='x' and capture the refusal; confirm NOTHING was persisted (no row, or the field left unset) — cleartext never lands
AGGREGATE guard: issue an analytics/group-by request that MIN/MAX/GROUP BYs f_secret (or f_password) and capture the rejection (a credential column is not aggregable — inference-oracle guard)
cross-check the negatives: scan every API response captured above and confirm no plaintext 'topsecret-value' / 'p@ssw0rd!' appears anywhere

acceptance.clause: secret WRITE stores ciphertext, never plaintext: after POSTing f_secret, the business row holds an opaque 'secret:<handle>' ref (SECRET_REF_PREFIX) — the plaintext is encrypted into sys_secret via the ICryptoProvider — and no API read echoes the written value
acceptance.verify: GET returns the mask, not 'topsecret-value'; where DB-inspectable, the column value starts with 'secret:' and sys_secret holds the ciphertext. engine.ts encryptSecretFields (cryptoProvider.encrypt → sys_secret → makeSecretRef); packages/objectql/src/secret-fields.ts
acceptance.evidence: the write response + the masked GET + (where available) the raw column / sys_secret excerpt

acceptance.clause: reads MASK for every reader: a GET of the record returns f_secret and f_password as SECRET_MASK '••••••••', not the written value — masking on the generic read path is unconditional (plaintext requires an explicit engine decrypt the API read never performs), so even a privileged reader gets the mask
acceptance.verify: both credential fields read back masked; collectMaskedReadFields (secret always; password unless managedBy:'better-auth'). Pinned by packages/qa/dogfood/test/field-zoo.matrix.ts kind:'masked' (f_secret, f_password) + packages/objectql/src/secret-fields.test.ts
acceptance.evidence: the masked GET + the pin output

acceptance.clause: an echoed mask is a NO-OP, not a clobber: PATCHing f_secret back as the SECRET_MASK sentinel drops the key and leaves the stored secret unchanged — a form round-trip that re-submits the mask does not wipe the secret
acceptance.verify: after the mask-PATCH the secret still resolves (mask on read, decrypts to the original where checked); engine.ts encryptSecretFields echoed-mask drop (value === SECRET_MASK ⇒ delete key)
acceptance.evidence: the mask-PATCH response + the post-PATCH read showing the secret intact

acceptance.clause: fail-CLOSED without a provider: with no ICryptoProvider registered, a non-empty f_secret write is REFUSED ('Refusing to store cleartext … fail-closed') and NOTHING is persisted — cleartext never reaches the business row; a `password` write needs no provider (plaintext at rest, masked on read)
acceptance.verify: the unwired-boot POST throws the fail-closed error and the row is absent/unset; engine.ts encryptSecretFields (`if (!this.cryptoProvider) throw`). No stock boot runs without a provider (fixtures.knownGaps[1]), so on stock this clause is recorded blocked(fixture); packages/objectql/src/secret-fields.test.ts 'fail-closed: writing a secret field with no CryptoProvider throws' is engine-layer evidence beside that verdict, never its pass (RUNNER rule 6, a pin scores only the layer it drives)
acceptance.evidence: the refusal + a GET/list confirming no persisted cleartext

acceptance.clause: a credential column cannot be AGGREGATED: a MIN/MAX/GROUP BY over f_secret or f_password is rejected unconditionally (even on a better-auth object) — an inference-oracle guard keyed off collectCredentialFields (ADR-0100 / #3171)
acceptance.verify: the group-by/aggregate request over the credential field returns a rejection, not a leaked value distribution; packages/objectql/src/secret-fields.ts collectCredentialFields

negative: any API read returning f_secret/f_password plaintext is a FAIL regardless of what the form shows
an f_secret write that persists cleartext to the business row — or succeeds at all with NO provider registered — is a FAIL (fail-open is exactly what ADR-0100 forbids)
a re-submitted SECRET_MASK that WIPES the stored secret is a FAIL (the echoed mask must be a no-op)
an aggregate over a credential column that returns a value distribution is a FAIL (inference oracle)

automated.ref: packages/qa/dogfood/test/field-zoo-roundtrip.dogfood.test.ts (+ field-zoo.matrix.ts masked vectors for f_secret & f_password) — acceptance[0] (its API oracle, the masked GET: knownGaps[2] makes the raw-column read the DB-inspectable extra), acceptance[1] and negative[0], at the HTTP door: the showcase is booted in-process, POST /data/showcase_field_zoo writes both fields, and GET /data/showcase_field_zoo/ID reads them back as SECRET_MASK, never the written value. packages/objectql/src/secret-fields.test.ts drives a real ObjectQL engine over a stub driver, with no HTTP, so it scores NO api clause of this item: it is engine-layer evidence beside acceptance[0]'s DB-inspectable leg ('encrypts on write: row stores a ref, sys_secret holds ciphertext, no cleartext on the row'), and for acceptance[2] ('update: echoing the read mask back does NOT overwrite the stored secret'), acceptance[3] ('fail-closed: writing a secret field with no CryptoProvider throws'), acceptance[4] (the 'objectql aggregate() rejects credential fields (ADR-0100 / #3171)' describe) and negative[1]–[3]. acceptance[2] and [4] are driven over the API; acceptance[3] is blocked(fixture) on every stock composition (knownGaps[1])

items.title: Import mapping TransformType matrix: each of the 7 declared transforms does exactly its documented conversion, javascript is refused loudly at the door (no sandbox), format mismatch is a named 400
personas: seeded admin (admin@objectos.ai / admin123) — holds manage_metadata for scratch mapping PUTs

the unknown-transform runtime refusal (import-mapping.ts) guards rows that arrive AROUND the parse seam — spec parse rejects an unknown value at authoring, so it is not HTTP-drivable end-to-end; it lives in the negative list, not a clause

variants: none — direct copy, also the default when `transform` is absent

items.title: A validation rule reads a parent field one hop through a lookup
personas: a member with create/edit on a child object and NO read on its lookup parent — the persona the rule exists to constrain. ⚠ No stock showcase persona is one (fixtures.knownGaps): acceptance[3] is scored from the engine pin or on a scratch pair

requires: showcase_invoice — carries the script validation no_invoice_for_churned_account, whose condition reads record.account.status one hop through the `account` lookup (examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/invoice.object.ts)
showcase_account — the referenced object; its `status` select carries the value 'churned' (examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/account.object.ts)
at least one churned account and one non-churned account to invoice against
knownGaps: No stock persona has showcase_invoice CRUD WITHOUT showcase_account read, and none can be provisioned. showcase_member_default, the everyone baseline every member holds, grants showcase_account allowRead (examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts), and permission sets only ever ADD grants, so no extra set takes it away (QA run #21720, parked on #22017 row 14). An earlier revision of this item said the opposite, reading packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-d3-d4-capabilities.dogfood.test.ts. That test's persona is its own injected fallback set, not a stock persona, and it never writes against a churned account. So acceptance[3] is scored from the ENGINE pin in `automated`, which proves the mechanism the clause rests on: the related row is read under SYSTEM authority with the acting identity carried, and the write path accepts and refuses by the parent field. A run that wants the live leg builds the scratch substitute #21720 measured: a scratch package with a parent object the member holds no grant on, and a child object (member create/edit) carrying a one-hop script validation over the lookup. Then it writes, as that member, against a tripping and a non-tripping parent

steps: POST /api/v1/data/showcase_invoice with `account` pointing at a NON-churned account
POST /api/v1/data/showcase_invoice with `account` pointing at a CHURNED account
PATCH an existing invoice to REPOINT it at a churned account (the update path reads the FK off the merged record, not the patch alone)
as a persona with NO read on the parent (none exists on stock — fixtures.knownGaps): run the engine pin, or on the scratch substitute write against a non-tripping parent, then a tripping one

acceptance.clause: the write PASSES when the parent field does not trip the rule — the traversal resolves, it does not fault
acceptance.verify: 2xx and the row is readable; the response carries no validation error, and in particular no 'could not be evaluated' fault
acceptance.evidence: the create response and the read-back

acceptance.clause: the write is REFUSED when the parent field trips the rule, carrying the AUTHORED message, not a fault
acceptance.verify: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED whose fields[] entry is { field: '_record', code: 'rule_violation' } and whose message is the rule's AUTHORED message — the one no_invoice_for_churned_account declares in the object metadata (the sentence about reactivating the account). A rule that evaluates true answers its authored message, not its name: the rule name appears in no field of the body (packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts). Score the code, the field and that the message equals the declared one; a refusal that reads 'could not be evaluated' is a FAIL, not a pass

acceptance.clause: a REPOINT on update is judged against the account the write lands on
acceptance.verify: the PATCH onto a churned account is refused even though the patch alone carries no status, because the FK is read off the merged record

acceptance.clause: a rule whose parent the acting user cannot read still ENFORCES, and still lets a legitimate write through — the read is system-authority, bounded by the fields the predicate names
acceptance.verify: on stock showcase no such persona exists (fixtures.knownGaps), so score this from the engine pin in `automated` or live on the scratch substitute. With such a persona, the non-churned write is 2xx and the churned write is 400 carrying the AUTHORED message; an unevaluable-rule envelope for this persona is the defect this clause exists to catch, and so is a 2xx on the churned account

items.title: Defaults that changed meaning on v18 (ADR-0087 D3 18.* entries): an omitted list-view page size is 50 (was 25), an omitted editInline means editable in place, an autonumber with no `unique` is unique per organization, and a field-heavy form opens as a bounded modal on desktop
personas: seeded admin (admin@objectos.ai / admin123) — the Default Organization owner and platform admin on a fresh boot

org member — created by the admin with POST /api/v1/auth/admin/create-user (stock showcase self-registration is closed: audience posture invite_only answers sign-up 403 SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED); joins the Default Organization as `member`, not platform admin, and lands mustChangePassword:true, i.e. a HELD session until it changes its password (POST /api/v1/auth/change-password). Neither stock demo persona is an updater on showcase_task: the updater is a member bound to the `contributor` position (allowEdit on showcase_task), whose task RLS (task_own_rows) shows only tasks assigned to it — so assign it some tasks first (admin PATCH assignee), QA runs #24558 / #24616

a showcase list view with no pagination.pageSize and no userActions.editInline (GET /api/v1/meta/view lists them)

steps: GET /api/v1/meta/view/VIEW to confirm the view declares no pagination and no userActions block — the meta read serves the authored view, so nothing resolved can be read there; the defaults show only in the renderer (the list request's top=50, the Edit inline switch). Open the list in the console and count the first page

as a member who may update, open the list and confirm the inline-edit affordance — the 'Edit inline' switch in the list's Display / view-settings popover at desktop width; as a read-only member confirm it is absent. The edit mode itself is session state that starts OFF (objectui app-shell ObjectView.tsx: 'The edit mode is now session state'), so cells are not editable on load until the switch is turned on — a click on a cell opens the record before then
create two rows of an autonumber object in the same org and read their numbers
open New on a field-heavy object on a desktop viewport, then on a mobile viewport

personas[1], fixtures.knownGaps[0], steps[0], steps[1] and acceptance[2].clause corrected from QA runs #24558 (5b14b7f3) and #24616 (ba4afcc2), re-read at objectstack f89d29e382 and the console pin 4016370af3c9. (1) knownGaps[0] was stale: the pinned console builds and was served. (2) The meta read serves the authored view, so step 1 has no resolved pageSize / editInline to read (`pagination` is an optional block; its pageSize default materialises only inside one); the defaults show in the renderer. (3) The inline affordance is the Edit inline switch, and the edit mode is session state that starts off (ObjectView.tsx), so 'offered' does not mean editable cells on load. (4) The updater persona needs a contributor binding and assigned tasks. Wave anchor #24579 round 2 §3 (6272314386)
